title: Design: Sales Type sits between Status and Location
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Scenario: A split work order was invoiced today at one of two locations, and you check where the Sales Type column sits.
  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • A second location, {Location-B}, is open to you, and the report shows its Location column.
    For example: {Location-B} is QA Testing, and both locations are selected in the Location filter.
  • Two active staff members at {Location-A} have their "Sales Representative" switch on: {Sales-rep-A} and {Sales-rep-B}.
    For example: {Sales-rep-A} is ZZAUTOTEST Ann Able and {Sales-rep-B} is ZZAUTOTEST Ben Able.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} at {Location-A} has "Sales Representative - Labor" {Sales-rep-A} and "Sales Representative - Parts" {Sales-rep-B} and was invoiced today.
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-40001.
  • The browser window is 1440 px wide with the zoom at 100%, and the design pictures "sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png" (board 4.9), "sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png" (board 4.11) and "sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png" (board 4.12) attached to this case are open beside it at 100% (actual size). Names, numbers and dates in the pictures are sample data.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Sales By Representative is open in that browser window, with the date range set to today and Show Unassigned on.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Turn the Sales Type column on in the column selector.
  2. Export the Expanded CSV and read the same headings.
  3. Export the Expanded PDF and read the same headings.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: a Sales Type column appears. Read from Status to the first money column, the headings read Status, Sales Type, Location, in that order (the picture of board 4.9 shows Sales Type straight after Status).
  • Step 2: the CSV headings read Status, Sales Type, Location, in that order.
  • Step 3: the PDF headings read Status, Sales Type, Location, in that order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R19: “An invoice row carries a "Sales Type" column, after Status and before Location (Status, Sales Type, Location), reading "Labor", "Parts", "Part Sales" or "Labor, Parts".”
  • S5-R23: “The Expanded CSV and the Expanded PDF always carry the Sales Type column, after Status and before Location, whatever the screen shows. In them, the cells of the side a row is not credited with are blank in the CSV and show a dash in the PDF.”

From: Chris Ward's answers, question sheet of 19 Oct 2026, Google Sheet 17Ry1BtRTPEkecBP5TlgAE0T93Ai1TQewdJ7B7WpWDBQ, tab "Questions for Chris", rows 6-43 (answered 19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 20 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 26: “26. (a) Status, Sales Type, Location.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Claude design canvas "Splitting Sales Representatives" (https://claude.ai/artifact/8MHqwyffAYtqZ6EccS5RUm), export read 19 Oct 2026, boards 4.9 Sales Type switched on; 4.11 Expanded export (CSV); 4.12 Expanded export (PDF) (the attached pictures are these boards).

Where the design and the PRD differ: The design draws one location only, so no board shows a Location column (boards 4.9 to 4.12 show Sales Type straight after Status). The order Status, Sales Type, Location comes from PRD v10 and Chris Ward's answer 26.

Design pictures attached to this case: sbr-09-a4-columns-on.png, sbr-11-a4-export-csv.png, sbr-12-a4-export-pdf-crop-1.png.

  • Design — board 4.9 title: “4.9 Sales Type switched on”
  • Design — board 4.9 note: “Switching it on adds the column next to Status.”
  • Design — board 4.11 title: “4.11 Expanded export (CSV)”
  • Design — board 4.11 note: “Downloaded with the Sales Type column switched off on screen: the file still has Sales Type (decision 40). An empty side is a blank cell. (Shown as a spreadsheet would open it.)”
  • Design — board 4.12 title: “4.12 Expanded export (PDF)”
  • Design — board 4.12 note: “The PDF always has the Sales Type column. An empty side shows a dash. Header lines name the filters, including "Sales Type: All".”
